newsitem.title: UK: Smith & Nephew profit up in tough markets.
newsitem.headline: Smith & Nephew profit up in tough markets.

text.p: Healthcare firm Smith & Nephew Plc, whose products range from sticking plasters to artificial knees, on Tuesday reported a slight increase in 1996 profit amid hefty competition and difficult market conditions.
Pre-tax profit before exceptional items rose to 182.2 million pounds ($295.7 million) from 180.4 million pounds, coming in at the lower end of analysts forecasts.
Currency strength had a modest impact on last year's results, but will make itself felt more if the dollar and pound stay at current levels, Smith & Nephew said.
The group said it planned to launch its promising human tissue skin replacement product Dermagraft in Britain and the U.S. in the second half of the year.
The launch in continental Europe will be staggered depending on different national regulatory requirements.

Smith & nephew said it maintained its share in all principal product and geographical markets. Strong unit growth was partially offset by price reductions, which were particularly severe in North America.
